skill.description: Provides GitHub Actions patterns for AI-assisted pull request review, issue triage, CI validation, and Git maintenance.

skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation-only, but several examples become high-risk if copied into GitHub Actions. Confirmed risks include dynamic exec-based git commands, privileged token use, untrusted comments entering shell and AI prompts, and a comment-triggered force-push path. Many static backtick, URL, and filesystem detections are Markdown or documentation false positives.

remediation.issue: Dynamic git commands interpolate commit, branch, and file values into shell strings.
remediation.suggestion: Use argv-based process APIs, validate commit hashes and branch names, quote paths safely, and avoid shell execution for git operations.

remediation.issue: The /rebase workflow can run privileged write actions from a pull request comment.
remediation.suggestion: Require maintainer permission checks, restrict GITHUB_TOKEN permissions, and require manual approval before force-pushing.

remediation.issue: AI prompts include pull request diffs, issue bodies, and comments from untrusted users.
remediation.suggestion: Treat all GitHub content as untrusted, add prompt-injection defenses, and keep AI output advisory until reviewed by a maintainer.

remediation.issue: Workflow examples use API keys and GitHub tokens without full scoping guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Document least-privilege permissions, never echo secrets, pin third-party actions, and separate read-only jobs from write-capable jobs.

semantic_findings.title: Comment-Triggered Rebase Lacks Authorization Checks
semantic_findings.description: The auto-rebase workflow triggers when a pull request comment contains /rebase, then uses GITHUB_TOKEN to checkout, rebase, and force-push. The example does not check maintainer association, team membership, or explicit repository permission before the write action.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The trigger condition, token usage, and force-push step are shown directly in the workflow. No authorization gate is shown in the cited job.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted GitHub Content Controls AI Outputs with Write Permissions
semantic_findings.description: PR diffs, issue bodies, and comments are inserted into AI prompts while workflows can write pull request reviews, labels, and issue comments. Malicious repository content or comments can prompt-inject the assistant and influence automated GitHub writes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited workflows combine untrusted GitHub text with AI prompts and GitHub write APIs. The skill does not show prompt-injection isolation or human approval gates for those writes.

content.value_statement: GitHub teams spend time repeating reviews, triage, testing decisions, and maintenance tasks. This skill provides AI-assisted workflow patterns for GitHub Actions, CI, and repository operations.
actual_capabilities: Outlines GitHub Actions workflows for AI pull request review and review comments.
Shows issue triage patterns for labels, severity, area, and initial responses.
Provides CI/CD examples for smart test selection and deployment risk checks.
Documents Git operation workflows for rebasing, cherry-picking, rollback, and branch cleanup.
Includes repository configuration examples for CODEOWNERS and branch protection.
Lists operational best practices for secrets, permissions, performance, and reliability.
limitations: Examples are patterns and require security review before use in production.
The skill does not validate organization policies, branch protections, or token scopes.
AI-generated labels, comments, and risk decisions can be wrong and need human oversight.
Some examples require GitHub CLI, GitHub Actions permissions, and external AI provider credentials.

use_cases.title: Automated Pull Request Review
use_cases.description: Create a workflow that summarizes diffs, flags risks, and posts review feedback on pull requests.

use_cases.title: Issue Intake and Labeling
use_cases.description: Classify new issues, suggest labels, detect missing reproduction steps, and draft a first response.

use_cases.title: CI and Repository Maintenance
use_cases.description: Select test suites, assess deployment risk, plan rollback automation, and identify stale branches.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Review Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for pull request review automation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub Actions workflow for AI pull request review. Use least-privilege permissions and explain the required secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Design Issue Triage
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for maintainers handling new issues.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an issue triage workflow that classifies type, severity, area, missing details, and recommended labels.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize CI Selection
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate CI/CD automation for larger repositories.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a smart test selection workflow for this repository. Map changed paths to test suites and include safe fallback behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Workflow Safety
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before deploying privileged automation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this GitHub automation for token scope, prompt injection, command injection, unsafe writes, and missing human approval gates.

output_examples.input: A pull request changes API handlers and database migrations.
output: A concise review summary for the changed areas.
A list of possible bugs, migration risks, and security concerns.

output_examples.input: A new issue reports a production error without reproduction steps.
output: Suggested labels for bug, priority, and affected area.
A short maintainer response requesting steps, expected behavior, actual behavior, and environment details.

output_examples.input: A deployment includes authentication and database changes.
output: Rollback checks to prepare before release.

best_practices: Use the smallest GitHub token permissions needed for each workflow job.
Treat pull request diffs, issue bodies, and comments as untrusted input.
Require human approval before workflows push commits, change labels, or affect deployments.
anti_patterns: Do not run comment-triggered write actions without checking the commenter permission level.
Do not pass secrets, private source, or sensitive logs to an AI provider without policy approval.
Do not build shell commands by interpolating branch names, commit hashes, or file paths.

faq.question: Does this skill install a GitHub App or workflow automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples that users must review and adapt.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it post pull request reviews?
faq.answer: It shows how to design workflows that post reviews, but the repository workflow must implement that behavior.

faq.question: Does it require secrets?
faq.answer: Many examples require an AI provider key or GitHub token stored in GitHub Secrets.

faq.question: Is it safe for public repositories?
faq.answer: It needs careful permission checks because public comments and pull requests are untrusted inputs.

faq.question: Can it replace maintainer review?
faq.answer: No. AI output should support maintainers, not approve changes or deployments without review.
